result:
I found 10 rules in `pricebook.py` whose code didn't match their docstrings (or the shared rules in the module docstring), and fixed all of them. After the fix, all 150 rules give exactly the same results as their docstrings over about 4,000 test combinations of quantity and unit price.

| Rule | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 13 | Discount was rounded with `round()`; the shared rule says to drop fractions below 1 won | `base * 15 // 100` |
| 14 | The 100,000-won cap only applied once the discount exceeded 200,000 won | Cap always applies: `min(disc, 100000)` |
| 21 | The cap was applied to the amount before the percentage, not to the discount | `(qty-12)*unit*3//100`, then `min(disc, 10000)` |
| 33 | Same as rule 14: the cap only applied above 200,000 won | `min(disc, 100000)` |
| 35 | Used 4% instead of 3% | `* 3 // 100` |
| 91 | Used `round()` (same as rule 13) | `base * 2 // 100` |
| 111 | Used `qty > 20`, so exactly 20 units got no discount even though the docstring says "20+" | `qty >= 20` |
| 115 | Used 16% instead of 15% | `* 15 // 100` |
| 137 | Used 9% instead of 8% | `* 8 // 100` |
| 138 | Used `round()` (same as rule 13) | `(qty - 20) * unit * 7 // 100` |

**How I checked:** I wrote a separate reference version of each rule built only from its docstring and the shared rules. I compared it with the real code for quantities 0–259 plus a few large values, and 15 unit prices. I also read every line that departs from the usual code pattern. Those lines in the other rules (for example `not qty < 50`, `50 <= qty`, `if disc > cap: disc = cap`) behave the same as the docstring.

- **Rule 72:** it uses `qty > 10`, but at exactly 10 units the discount on units above 10 is 0 either way, so the result is the same. I left it unchanged.

There are no tests in the repository, so this comparison is the only check that was run. I kept the original file at `/tmp/chk/pricebook.orig.py`.

STATUS: DONE
